deals.evidence: Chinese businessman Jisheng Gao and his family have completed a deal to buy 80% of Southampton.
deals.headline: Gao Jisheng's family buys 80% of Southampton
deals.summary: Chinese businessman Jisheng Gao and his family completed the purchase of 80% of the club as a personal investment; Katharina Liebherr kept 20%. The price is not stated on the cited page.

deals.evidence: the Group gained access to a term loan totalling Ê78.8m immediately prior to the Statement of Financial Position date
deals.headline: Southampton take a £78.8m term loan to cover pandemic losses
deals.investor: MSD (MSD UK Holdings Limited as security agent)
deals.source_name: St Mary's Football Group Limited financial statements, year ended 30 June 2020 (southamptonfc.com)
deals.summary: The group drew a £78.8m term loan just before 30 June 2020, replacing its working capital facility; the charges register shows security created on 29-30 June 2020 in favour of MSD UK Holdings Limited as security agent, and later accounts call it the Group's facility with MSD.

deals.evidence: sold the entire share capital of St Mary's Football Group Limited to Sport Republic Limited and Katharina Liebherr, who have become the immediate owners.
deals.headline: Sport Republic and Katharina Liebherr buy St Mary's Football Group from Lander Sports
deals.investor: Sport Republic (Dragan Šolak, Rasmus Ankersen, Henrik Kraft) with Katharina Liebherr
deals.seller: Lander Sports (UK) International Investment Co., Ltd (Gao Jisheng)
deals.source_name: St Mary's Football Group Limited financial statements, year ended 30 June 2021 (southamptonfc.com)
deals.summary: Lander Sports sold the entire share capital of the club's parent, St Mary's Football Group, to Sport Republic and Katharina Liebherr; Dragan Šolak became the ultimate controlling party. The price is not disclosed in the accounts.

deals.evidence: the facility was uplifted back to £80,000,000 and has been fully drawn
deals.headline: Southampton refinance MSD facility, uplifted back to £80m
deals.source_name: St Mary's Football Group Limited financial statements, year ended 30 June 2024 (southamptonfc.com)
deals.summary: After the 2023-24 year end the group refinanced its facility with MSD on better interest, repayment and covenant terms and the facility was uplifted back to £80m and fully drawn; a charge over the St Mary's Stadium property in favour of MSD Investment Corp. was created on 20 September 2024.

name: Southampton Football Club
notes: Revenue and the 2024-25 facts come from St Mary's Football Group's group accounts to 30 June 2025 as filed at Companies House (approved November 2025). That PDF is a scanned image with no text layer, so the evidence phrases were read off the page image and an automated text match on that URL will fail; the club's own Financial Statements page has not yet posted 2024-25 and offers the 2023-24 accounts as text (turnover £84,775k, net debt £57.5m). The June 2020 accounts' text layer renders £ as 'Ê' (evidence copied as it extracts). Stakes: shares are given as counts on the July 2026 confirmation statement; no page states percentages, so stake_pct is null (Sport Republic UK is the 75%+ PSC of the parent). The June 2026 allottee is not named. Southampton were expelled from the 2026 Championship play-offs over 'Spygate' and start 2026-27 on minus four points (BBC). Chair, wages total (only the men's first-team player pay of £83.2m and a 73.2% all-staff wages-to-turnover ratio are stated), attendance, social counts and the price paid by Sport Republic in 2021-22 not found on citable pages. No valuation published.

ownership_summary: Controlled by Serbian businessman Dragan Šolak through Sport Republic, the sports investment firm founded by Rasmus Ankersen and Henrik Kraft that bought the club's parent, St Mary's Football Group, from Gao Jisheng's Lander Sports with Katharina Liebherr on 22 December 2021. At the July 2026 confirmation statement Sport Republic UK Ltd held 100,340 and Katharina Liebherr 10,000 of St Mary's Football Group's ordinary shares; Šolak holds 75% or more of Sport Republic Holding Ltd, and Ankersen remains a co-owner.
